_comment: The one capability catalogue for the website and the Android app. Edit this file; web/feature-pages.js embeds it (node scripts/sync-feature-catalog.mjs) and Android packages it from shared/. Statuses: WORKING (implemented, connected, verified), PARTIAL (some real functionality; the note says what it depends on), PLANNED (designed, not active), UNSUPPORTED (no route on that platform). Nothing on Android is WORKING until a real-device run is recorded.

how: Type or speak a request.

web.summary: Control supported phone actions using natural language.
web.what: Phone Agent runs on-device skills in the ZARVIS Android app: the actions listed below. Each one asks for the Android access it needs first, and a call waits for you to confirm the exact number. It opens settings screens but does not change settings for you.
web.why: Common phone actions stay in the same conversation as the rest of ZARVIS, on a device that can actually perform them.
how: You say or type a supported command on the Android app.
ZARVIS matches an on-device skill.
If the action needs a permission or confirmation, it asks first.
The phone performs only that action.
web.start: On the Android app, open Phone Agent and try a command below. The website cannot place calls or open your apps.
web.permissions: Each phone action on this page says what it needs. Android asks for runtime permissions such as Phone, Contacts and Location; Notification access, Usage access and the accessibility service are turned on by you in Android Settings.
limits: These actions run only in the Android app.
The website can show the commands. It cannot run them.
None of them is marked Working until it has been checked on a real phone.
examples: Open WhatsApp
Find Mom's number

android.summary: Control supported phone actions using natural language.
android.what: Phone Agent uses on-device skills: open apps, find contacts, place a call after you confirm the exact number, set reminders, hand an alarm to the Clock app, open a pre-filled calendar event, pick a document or photo, take a photo, show your approximate location, open Bluetooth, Wi-Fi or location settings, summarize or speak notifications under your privacy rules, show today's screen time, navigate by voice (Back, Home, notifications, lock screen) and read or tap the app you're using through its accessibility service. It does not change settings for you.
android.why: Supported phone actions stay in the same conversation as the rest of ZARVIS.
how: Say or type a supported command.
ZARVIS explains any access it needs first (Allow / Not now / Learn more), then Android asks.
Calls show the exact name and number and wait for your confirmation.
Hand-offs (Clock, calendar, settings) finish in that app — ZARVIS tells you when you need to act there.
android.start: Try a command below. Nothing runs until you send it.
android.permissions: Calls need Phone; a contact name also needs Contacts. Reminders need notifications. Location needs approximate location. Reading or speaking notifications needs Notification access; screen time needs Usage access; voice navigation and screen reading need ZARVIS's accessibility service — you turn each of these on yourself in Android Settings. Pickers, camera, calendar and settings use system screens and need no permission. See Settings › Permissions & Device Access.
limits: Only the actions listed here are implemented, and none is verified on a real device yet.
ZARVIS never changes Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or other settings itself — it opens the screen for you.
Accessibility is used only for the single action you ask for and confirm — never general automation, never inside banking, password, Android Settings or permission screens.
There is no wake word: the assistant gesture opens ZARVIS only when you choose ZARVIS as the default assistant.
examples: Open WhatsApp
Find Mom's number
Remind me to drink water in 30 minutes
Open bluetooth settings

web.summary: Search, compare, and outline a topic from the chat workspace.
web.what: Web search looks up live results through the backend. Research skills write a comparison, report, or outline from general knowledge and say when that answer is not live-sourced.
web.why: You can ask for a short answer or a structured overview without leaving the conversation.
how: Ask a question in Chat.
Search is used when the request needs live web information.
Compare, report, and outline skills reason over general knowledge.
Those replies are labeled when they are not from a live source.
canDo: Research outline of questions worth investigating
web.start: Tap a prompt, add your topic, and send it from Chat.
web.permissions: No device permission. Search uses the configured backend provider.
limits: Research compare, report, and outline are not live web fetches.
Search results depend on the provider configured on the server.
examples: Search the web for the latest information about:
Research this topic and give me a structured overview:
Compare these options:
web.prompt: Research this topic and give me a structured overview, key points, and questions worth investigating:

android.summary: Search, compare, and outline a topic from chat.
android.what: Web search uses the backend. Research compare, report, and outline use general knowledge and say when the answer is not live-sourced.
android.why: A short answer or a structured overview stays in one conversation.
how: Ask in Chat.
Search is used for live web information.
Compare, report, and outline are not live fetches.
android.start: Edit the prompt with your topic, then send it.
limits: Research replies are not live web fetches.
Search depends on the server provider.
examples: Search the web for the latest information about:
android.prompt: Research this topic and give me a structured overview, key points, and questions worth investigating:

web.summary: Attach a file and ask ZARVIS to summarize or explain it.
web.what: You choose a file. ZARVIS reads the text and can summarize it or answer questions about that text in the same chat.
web.why: A long document can be reduced to the points you need, in the language you ask for.
how: Tap the attach control in Chat.
Choose a supported file.
The file name appears above the composer.
Send your question. The attachment is included with that message.
canDo: Ask follow-up questions about the attached text
web.start: Open Chat, attach a file, and send a question such as “Summarize this.”
web.permissions: The file picker opens only when you tap Attach. Nothing is read from your device before that.
limits: Supported types include PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD, CSV, JSON, and common images (PNG, JPEG, WEBP).
The attachment is sent with the next message, then cleared.
Summary quality follows the configured AI provider.
examples: Summarize this document in simple language
What are the action items in this file?
Explain the important numbers
web.prompt: I will attach a document. Summarize it clearly and explain the important points in simple language.

android.summary: Ask ZARVIS to summarize or explain text you provide.
android.what: The document skill summarizes text you share. On the web you attach PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD, CSV, JSON, or a common image. This Android chat accepts the request in text.
android.why: A long document can be reduced to the points you need.
how: Share the text or attach the file on the web.
Ask for a summary or a question about it.
android.start: Send a prompt, then include the text you want summarized.
android.permissions: Files are read only when you choose them. The Android app does not scan storage for this skill.
limits: Summary quality follows the configured AI provider.
examples: Summarize this document in simple language
android.prompt: I will share a document. Summarize it clearly and explain the important points in simple language.

web.summary: Draft messages, poems, and idea lists in the tone you ask for.
web.what: Creative skills write a message, a poem, or a brainstorm from your prompt. They use the same chat as everything else.
web.why: A first draft is faster to edit than to start from a blank page.
how: Describe what you want, including tone and length.
ZARVIS drafts it in Chat.
Ask for a revision in the next message.
web.start: Start from a prompt below and edit the details before sending.
limits: Drafts are generated text, not a published post or a sent message.
Output follows the configured AI provider, or an honestly labeled fallback when no provider key is set.
examples: Write a warm birthday message for a friend
Brainstorm names for a weekend project
Write a short poem about rain
web.prompt: Help me create something polished. Start by asking what I want to make, then draft it for me.

how: Describe tone and length.
Review the draft in Chat.
Ask for a revision.
android.start: Edit the prompt, then send it.

web.what: Business skills that exist today: a social post, a customer reply, and an invoice draft parsed from line items you type.
web.why: Everyday business writing starts from a structured draft you can copy and edit.
how: Say which draft you need.
Include the facts: product, customer, or line items.
Review the draft in Chat before you use it.
canDo: Invoice draft from line items you provide
web.start: Open Chat with a business prompt and replace the placeholder with your details.
web.permissions: No device permission. Drafts are not sent to customers or posted anywhere.
limits: ZARVIS does not publish, email, or collect payment.
The invoice draft is a document, not a filed invoice.
Do not treat a draft as legal or tax advice.

Draft an invoice for these items:

web.summary: Read a repository, then change it only after you confirm.
web.what: Repository analysis is read-only. Implementation can create a branch and a pull request on GitHub, and it requires an explicit confirmation. It does not merge.
web.why: You can inspect a project from chat, and keep code changes behind a confirmation step.
how: Share a repository URL and ask for analysis.
ZARVIS reports what it can see.
A code change is a separate, confirmed action.
Review the pull request before anything is merged.
canDo: Pull request creation when that action is confirmed
web.start: Open Developer Agent, paste a repository URL and run Analyze. Implement shows the exact pull request for your approval before anything is written.
web.permissions: Implementation uses the protected developer workflow and your confirmation. Analysis does not change the repository.
limits: Implement needs a {{PRO plan|plans}} and your own {{connected GitHub account|developer}}.
Nothing is merged automatically.
The Android Developer screen is read-only analysis.
examples: Analyze this repository and tell me what needs fixing:
What is the build system of this repo?
web.prompt: I want help with my GitHub project. I will provide the repository URL. Analyze it first and tell me what needs fixing.

android.summary: Read a repository. Code changes stay behind confirmation.
android.what: The Android Developer screen analyzes a repository URL. It does not change code. Implementation on the server requires an explicit confirmation and is not a button on this screen.
android.why: You can inspect a project without a silent write.
how: Open Developer Agent.
Paste a repository URL.
Run Analyze.
Read the summary.
android.start: Open Developer Agent. Analyze does not modify the repository.
android.permissions: No phone permission. Analysis is read-only in this app.
limits: Pull requests are not offered on this screen.
Nothing is merged automatically.
examples: https://github.org/example/repository

android.summary: Create a trackable task, then follow, pause or cancel it.
android.what: You can create a task from Chat and follow it in Work › Tasks. Creating a task stores its steps. On the phone you can pause or cancel it; running a step is on the website for now.
android.why: A multi-step goal stays visible after you leave the chat.
how: Describe the goal in Chat.
Open Work › Tasks to see its status, pause it or cancel it.
A created task is tracking, not completed work.
android.start: Create a task from Chat, then review it in Work › Tasks.
android.permissions: Uses your ZARVIS account. Scheduled reminders use Android notifications when you create one.
limits: Steps don't run from the phone yet; run them on the website.
A reminder that notifies you is a Phone Agent action, not a task.
examples: Create a workflow for this goal and break it into clear steps:
android.prompt: Create a workflow for this goal and break it into clear steps:
